286491924_f2e9799b.text: Principal retinorecipient neurons of mouse dLGN are thalamocortical relay cells (TRCs) (Guido, 2018). These excitatory neurons make up the majority (80%-90%) of neurons in dLGN and can be divided into three morphologically distinct types: W-like TRCs which are hemispheric in shape, X-like TRCs which are biconical in shape, and Y-like TRCs which are radially symmetrical in shape (Krahe et al., 2011). While axons from distinct types of RGCs appear to project into a "hidden" laminar organization within mouse dLGN (Martin, 2004)(Reese, 1988)(Hong et al., 2011), the three types of TRCs do not demonstrate clear laminar distribution. Instead, W- like cells occupy the shell region of dLGN, while X-and Y-like cells occupy the core of the mouse dLGN (Krahe et al., 2011).
